clue.text: Character in front of the bars at the Albert Hall in summer?

definitions.text: Character in front of the bars at the Albert Hall in summer?

parts.words: Character in front of the bars at the Albert Hall in summer
parts.note: the bars are musical bars, not pubs, and the Proms concerts fill the Albert Hall each summer; the musical symbol written at the start of the staff for upper parts

explanation.surface: Someone loitering outside the pubs near the Royal Albert Hall on a summer evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person and 'bars' drinking places; here the character is a written symbol and the bars are measures of music. The Albert Hall hosts the Proms, London's summer classical concert season.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol placed at the start of a stave of music, before the first measure, fixing pitch for higher voices and instruments.

clue.text: Candid female blasting off in row

indicators.note: the abbreviation is launched away, removed from the word

parts.note: frank means candid

explanation.surface: An outspoken woman sounding off in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' seems to mean a quarrel; it is a line, as in a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A line or tier of things, as in the front rank of soldiers.

clue.text: Grumble about the Left taking independent standpoint

indicators.note: the complaint word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint

explanation.surface: A political complaint about the Left adopting an independent position.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or conviction someone holds, a position on an issue.

clue.text: Charge hospital department with evidence of neglect?

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
rust shows metal has been neglected

explanation.surface: Accusing a hospital ward of neglectful care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like accuse; it means hand over responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a duty or something to look after, as in charge with a task.

clue.text: Fifty absent (half missing) in places of work

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty

indicators.note: half of the word is missing, leaving its first three letters

explanation.surface: Fifty workers off sick, leaving the workplaces half empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories, where scientists do their work.

clue.text: Opportunities for celebration if seats can be arranged

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Parties can go ahead if seating can be organised.
explanation.definitionFit: Festivals or holidays, especially in Spanish-speaking places, are occasions for celebrating.

clue.text: Sculptor, merry one? Oh, that's unusual!

indicators.note: unusual signals the preceding letters taken in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if an artist is cheerful and finds it surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A twentieth-century English artist famous for large reclining stone and bronze figures.

clue.text: Quiet female leading old chaps on — remarkable thing

parts.note: p is piano, the musical mark for quiet
a hen is a female bird
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken woman leading a group of old men onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraordinary or a prodigy, as in a phenomenal talent.

clue.text: Component of alphabet (Hebrew)

indicators.note: a component is a part, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A simple description of one letter in the Hebrew script.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'alphabet' and the start of 'Hebrew', and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Hebrew script, equivalent to B, so it is literally one part of that alphabet.

clue.text: Novel final item of furniture that can be blown up

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the word final is given a new arrangement

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A last piece of furniture in a book turns out to be one that inflates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it signals rearranging FINAL to INFLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something filled with air to expand it is described by this adjective, as with a dinghy or mattress.

clue.text: Winter sports feature has a Parisian faced with terrible risk

indicators.note: the second piece is fronted by the first, so the jumble comes first
terrible here describes the word risk as badly mangled, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A slope at a resort comes with a frightening danger for a French visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges RISK to SKIR, which faces UN, the French 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or track prepared for skiers is a typical part of a winter resort.

clue.text: Swimmer making money one paper's written about inside

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes within the word for money

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the pair is set down backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A fish story: someone earns cash with a piece a newspaper ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns one and paper round, 'inside' sets them in the money; the FT (Financial Times) is the usual crossword paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiskered freshwater fish, so a creature that swims; crosswords often call fish swimmers.

clue.text: County with no barrier round — no real sign of alien invasion!

definitions.text: no real sign of alien invasion

indicators.note: the barrier word is dropped from the county

parts.note: Cornwall is a county in south-west England
a wall is a barrier
a circle is a round

explanation.surface: An unfenced field in a county hosts strange markings blamed on aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNWALL is England's south-westernmost county; removing WALL leaves CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattened patterns in crop fields often blamed on visiting spacecraft, though they are not genuine evidence.

clue.text: Capture sound of excited actor and daughter hugging French relation

indicators.note: the outer letters embrace the relation
excited suggests the letters stirred up into a new order

parts.note: pere is French for father

explanation.surface: An excited actor hugs his daughter and French relation on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives TACOR; the French relation is a father, and 'hugging' sets him after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve audio on magnetic tape, so to capture it for playback.

clue.text: Everyone to be accommodated in empty houses or rooms

indicators.note: the word for everyone is given lodging inside the other letters
empty removes the inside, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone must be housed in vacant homes or spare rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Large public rooms or corridors, such as a dining or concert hall.

clue.text: Top man, I will be standing by mother

parts.note: Max is a man's name
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A leading man says he will stand by his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' looks like one phrase; only 'Top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest possible amount or highest level, as in a top speed.

clue.text: Wine and fish Eastern maiden served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: cod is a fish
M is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A meal of wine and fish brought to the table by a young woman from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses the pieces in this down entry. A maiden over in cricket is one with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A red Bordeaux from the area of that name in south-west France.

clue.text: Stories lacking freshness, start to finish

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken from the start and moved to the end

parts.note: stale food or ideas lack freshness

explanation.surface: Tired old stories told from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the S of STALE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Narratives or yarns, plural like the clue word.

clue.text: Rex inclined to be ecstatic

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
apt means inclined or likely to

explanation.surface: A dog called Rex seems inclined to be overjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: R for Rex (king) is a regular crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely absorbed or enraptured, close to the sense of being in raptures.

clue.text: Firm favoured making bit of money

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
in means fashionable or favoured

explanation.surface: A popular company is making a small profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal piece of currency is a small unit of cash.

clue.text: Thrive, making pounds in time of prosperity

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits within the word for good times

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic growth
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Doing well, earning money while the economy flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or be at one's peak, as a flower in full blossom.

clue.text: Oxford college attendant gives edict: Do good

parts.note: a bull is a papal edict
taken as written

explanation.surface: A college porter issues an order to behave well.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a bulldog is a university proctor's attendant who helps keep discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: The name for an Oxford proctor's assistant, an official who helps police undergraduate behaviour.

clue.text: Something on the floor, security device in town

parts.note: a mat lies on the floor
a lock secures a door

explanation.surface: A doormat and a lock found in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: MATLOCK is a spa town in Derbyshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Derbyshire market and spa town in the English Peak District.

clue.text: Peculiar scoundrel with admissions of debt

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An odd rogue who keeps signing notes promising to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or odd, the sense in 'a curious thing happened'.

clue.text: Where to eat from tin with adolescent

parts.note: a can is a tin
a teen is a teenager

explanation.surface: A teenager eating straight out of a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining room in a workplace, school or barracks where meals are served.

clue.text: Stand-in worker joins the French place of worship

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker standing in
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An agency worker takes a job at a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: A building for religious worship, especially in non-Christian faiths.

clue.text: Green I spotted between river and lake — spring back

indicators.note: the pieces are seen placed between the two map abbreviations

parts.note: eco- means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: An environmentalist sees something by the water and jumps away in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted between' puts ECO and I between R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump or flinch backwards, as a gun does on firing.

clue.text: Excellent group of caring Christians set up in lots of countries

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the letters to read from the bottom

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian charity

explanation.surface: A fine Christian charity established across many nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses AI and SA. A1 (here AI) means first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent, which contains a great many nations.

clue.text: Tennis player of yesteryear in a work of fiction

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A former tennis star appears in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ashe won Wimbledon in 1975; SHE is Rider Haggard's adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe, the American champion of the 1960s and 70s, a player from the past.

clue.text: Upset male model after party

indicators.note: the remaining pieces follow the party word

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A male model is upset after a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to unsettle or disturb someone's calm.

clue.text: Bird's bit of fun

definitions.meaning: a songbird such as the skylark
a prank or frolic, done for a laugh

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a songbird and a playful escapade.

clue.text: Hugo Allen is such a footballer!

definitions.text: Hugo Allen is such a footballer!

parts.words: Hugo Allen is such a footballer
parts.note: the name Hugo Allen keeps the word goal inside it, across the two names, which makes it a keeper of that word

explanation.surface: A fan admiring a player called Hugo Allen.
explanation.walkthrough: Look at the letters: huGO ALlen holds GOAL, so the name is a keeper of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The player who guards the net in soccer, here given a punning reading as one who holds a goal.
